title: Safety-preview slider and impact band for batching + cache recommendations
creator: Sofia Alvarez
description: Design a compact, inline preview panel that surfaces recommended batching and prefix/KV caching changes alongside a safety slider and impact bands. The goal is to let engineers/operators preview cost/latency/quality trade-offs before applying recommended policies and to provide clear rollback and canary rollout actions. The panel should live in the Routes -> Optimization tab and be accessible via the existing 'Advisor' quick actions.
background: Field research and support tickets show teams are hesitant to adopt automated batching/cache recommendations because they cannot easily preview downstream quality impact and rollback steps. Existing designs focus on presets and static recommendations; this ticket explores a risk-aware preview control (safety slider) with visual confidence bands and simulated token-economy lens.
design_notes: Three primary states: Preview (simulation only), Canary (10-25% traffic), and Apply (full rollout)
Safety slider adjusts aggressiveness of recommendations (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive)
Impact bands show projected cost savings and latency change with 90% confidence intervals based on historical workload distribution
Inline QA sample: show 3 random prompt/response pairs and a delta score for quality regressions (BLEU-ish or custom eval metric)
Include explicit fallback guidance: compatible model variants, KV cache TTLs, and prefix-match heuristics
Accessible color palette and microcopy for risk explanation (avoid jargon)
Compact layout target: fits within a 560x380 modal or a 320px-wide right rail card
acceptance_criteria: Prototype in Figma with interactive slider states (Conservative/Balanced/Aggressive) linked to simulated numeric outputs
Simulated preview shows: projected token cost per 1M requests, median latency change, and quality delta with confidence band
Canary flow mock shows granular traffic percentage control, automatic rollback trigger options, and a canary health check card
UX copy for safety microcopy reviewed by PM and Support and included in the mock
Design handoff tokens: component specs, responsive constraints, and accessibility notes delivered to Engineering
Usability test (5 internal PLG engineers) with task completion rate >= 80% for preview->canary flow
decisions: Keep safety slider with three discrete stops instead of continuous control after research feedback favored mental model clarity
Surface a single composite recommendation by default, with advanced toggles for per-route overrides
Use historical 90% confidence intervals computed by backend; UI will label as 'simulated'
Show QA sample only when model eval data exists for the route; otherwise display 'preview unavailable' guidance
